subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — stabilization band, packaging credits & proposed redline
messages:
-----Original Message-----
From: Elena Morales <procurement@novexhealth.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Harry Song <harry.song@novexhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing exhibit — initial redline and packaging questions

Chloe,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Attached is Novex's initial redline with comments on Exhibit B (pricing bands), plus an Excel with our projected monthly token profile. High-level asks:

- We need a hard floor for the baseline committed band but want a 10% seasonal buffer for clinical trials (months 6–9).
- The proposed "stabilizer" clause is unclear on how credits accrue if we dip below the floor during a calendar quarter. We asked for a quarterly true-up approach instead of monthly reconciliations.
- Packaging credits: for bundled models (embed + chat) we requested a stacking credit — 12% off combined unit rate above 250M tokens/month.
- If Redwood requires a minimum cap on burst capacity, please explain how that interacts with Dedicated pooling.

We attached two files: Novex_pricing_redline_v1.docx and exhibit-B-band-matrix.xlsx. Please review and tell us what is reasonable for Redwood to accept. We are aiming to finalize commercial terms this month.

Best,
Elena Morales\Head of Procurement\Novex Health

---

On Fri, 20 Nov 2026 at 10:05 AM, chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com wrote:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <procurement@novexhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — initial redline and packaging questions

Elena — thanks for the detailed redline and the traffic matrix. We've had an internal pass and below are clarifying points and the items we think are negotiable versus those that need a constrained wording.

1) Floor + seasonal buffer
- We can accept a defined seasonal buffer but prefer a banded approach: maintain the committed floor, allow a temporary -10% buffer for up to three consecutive months once per 12-month period (to capture trial bursts).
- If you need a quarterly true-up instead of monthly, that's acceptable provided the annual true-up calculation preserves minimum revenue expectations for Redwood.

2) Stabilizer credits
- Our stabilizer language intends credits to accrue only when usage in a quarter falls below the floor and the customer has an active committed band. Credits are applied against future consumption up to 12 months.
- We cannot make credits refundable outside of offsets to future usage.

3) Packaging stacking credit
- We are open to a cross-product stacking credit but need to limit it to combined consumption above a defined threshold and cap the cumulative discount at 15% to protect unit economics.

4) Burst capacity & Dedicated pool interaction
- For Dedicated customers, burst capacity is priced as metered overage with a capped monthly surcharge. We can include a carveout that allows Novex to reserve a pre-paid burst buffer that does not count against committed minimums.

I copied Ben (pricing) and Karthik (order-schedule mapping) to help scope precise redline language. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the Exhibit B matrix? If you upload a second version of the redline with line-number references, Ben can provide a markup faster.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin\Account Director, Strategic Accounts\Redwood Inference\cell: 415-555-0126

Attachment: redwood_response_notes.txt (summary of internal positions)

---

On Mon, 22 Nov 2026 at 09:17 AM, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <procurement@novexhealth.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — proposed compromise language (redline attached)

Elena, Chloe — following our quick sync this morning, we've incorporated a compromise redline addressing the main asks. Key points in Novex_pricing_redline_v2 (attached):

- Seasonal Buffer: Added a defined Seasonal Buffer clause in Exhibit B allowing one 90-day buffer window per 12-month period reducing the committed floor by up to 10% without penalty. The clause requires Novex to designate the buffer window at least 14 days in advance.
- Quarterly True-up: Replaced monthly reconciliations with a quarterly true-up mechanism; shortfalls in a quarter will be credited as non-refundable usage credits applied against future consumption within 12 months.
- Stacking Credit: Introduced a cross-product stacking credit tier that applies a 12% blended reduction when combined consumption for chat+embedding exceeds 250M tokens in a month; cumulative cap set at 15% per invoice to preserve margin.
- Burst Reservation: Added a pre-paid burst buffer option for Dedicated customers — reserved capacity is billed as a separate line item and excluded from the committed floor calculation.

I've attached Novex_pricing_redline_v2.docx and a revised Exhibit-B-band-matrix.xlsx that maps the credit tiers. Legal reviewed the language to avoid giving refundable credits or multi-year revenue exposure.

Next steps: if Novex is comfortable with v2, we can generate an order-form with the redlined Exhibit B and push to DocuSign. If any of the caps (15%) or the pre-pay buffer structure are blockers, please highlight which specific clause and we'll flag for a rapid exec review.

Regards,
Ben Carter\Head of Pricing Analytics\Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novex_pricing_redline_v2.docx, exhibit-B-band-matrix_v2.xlsx

---

On Mon, 22 Nov 2026 at 16:04:00 -0800, Elena Morales <procurement@novexhealth.com> wrote:
From: Elena Morales <procurement@novexhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Harry Song <harry.song@novexhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — proposed compromise language (redline attached)

Ben/Chloe,

Thank you — we've reviewed v2 and the language looks materially acceptable. A couple of final clarifications before we ask legal to sign off:

1) Seasonal buffer notice period: 14 days is workable but Novex requests an automatic exception for unplanned public health trial surges where notice can't be provided. We proposed language that allows the buffer to be invoked retroactively up to one event per year with explanation.
2) Stacking credit floor: confirm that the 250M threshold is calculated on total monthly billable tokens across all regions and that inter-region routing won't split the tally.
3) Burst reservation invoice treatment: please confirm whether pre-paid burst buffers can be amortized monthly or must be recognized up-front on purchase. Our auditors prefer amortization.

If you can confirm those three points in writing we will send this to Novex legal and loop DocuSign. Otherwise this looks good and we appreciate the pragmatic caps on cumulative discounts.

Best,
Elena Morales\Head of Procurement\Novex Health

---

Notes: Redwood internal action items: (1) legal to confirm retroactive buffer wording risk exposure; (2) finance to provide amortization treatment options for pre-paid burst buffer; (3) operations to confirm cross-region token aggregation behavior.
